title: Comprehensive Ocular Manifestations of CMV and HIV
summary: An exhaustive clinical guide to the ophthalmic complications of Cytomegalovirus and HIV, covering anterior and posterior segment diseases, diagnostic markers like CD4+ counts, and evolving treatment paradigms in the era of Antiretroviral Therapy (ART).

sections.title: CMV: Anterior Uveitis & Endotheliitis
content: Anterior Uveitis (Immunocompetent): Occurs in healthy individuals; increasingly recognized as a cause of unilateral, hypertensive uveitis.
Clinical Features: Unilateral, usually with increased Intraocular Pressure (iIOP). Note: There may be no obvious iris atrophy, distinguishing it from HSV or VZV.
Corneal Endotheliitis (Commoner in Far East): Focal (coin-shaped) to diffuse bullous keratopathy.
Endotheliitis Signs: Stromal corneal oedema, Keratic Precipitates (KPs) of variable appearance.
Anterior Chamber (AC) Inflammation: Usually mild with no Posterior Synechiae (PS); ± diffuse iris atrophy and iIOP.
Treatment: Often challenging; may respond to oral valganciclovir. IOP control can be difficult.

sections.title: HIV: Global Epidemiology & Stats (2015-2016)
sections.content: HIV (HIV-1 and 2) is an RNA retrovirus infecting CD4+ T-cells. Statistics: 736.7 million people living with HIV end of 2015. ART expansion reduced deaths to 1.1 million in 2015 (45% fewer than 2005). Over 18 million were on ART by mid-2016. Most cases are in developing countries (sub-Saharan Africa) linked to socio-economic deprivation. Transmission: blood, bodily fluids, unprotected sex, IV drug abuse, transfusions, and vertical transmission.

sections.title: CD4 Levels and Typical Ocular Disease
Disease Markers & Management
content: Markers: CD4 level (immunocompromise/susceptibility indicator) and Viral Load (RNA copies/mL, risk of progression).
ART Regimen: At least 3 drugs—usually 2 nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors + 1 protease inhibitor or non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor.
Coordination: Care must be shared between an experienced HIV ophthalmologist and an HIV physician.

sections.title: HIV Anterior Segment Conditions
content: Conjunctival Microvasculopathy: Common; irregular-calibre vessels, often in a corkscrew pattern; may associate with retinal microvasculopathy.
VZV Keratouveitis: Common; may lack HZO rash. Features: moderate anterior uveitis, iIOP, iris atrophy. Rx: Systemic aciclovir/famciclovir.
HSV Keratouveitis: Equal prevalence to general population but more severe in HIV; limbal, more recurrences, larger/less defined dendrites. Rx: Topical ± systemic antiviral.
Microsporidial Keratouveitis: Bilateral irritation, photophobia, punctate keratopathy, follicular conjunctivitis, and/or anterior uveitis.
Anterior Uveitis: Seen in >50% of HIV patients. VZV/HSV cause mild inflammation with iIOP. Posterior uveitis (Toxo/Syphilis) also causes AC inflammation.
Drug-Induced Uveitis: Caused by Rifabutin (anti-atypical mycobacteria) and Cidofovir (anti-CMV).

branches: Granular Retinitis: Indolent, minimal haemorrhage, no vascular sheathing
Perivascular Retinitis: 'Frosted branch angiitis' following retinal vessels

sections.title: Specific Anti-CMV Treatment Protocols
content: Prophylaxis: Sustain CD4 count >50/mm3 via ART.
Induction Therapy: Initial high-dose treatment to control active infection.
Maintenance Therapy: Lifelong treatment if immune recovery does not occur.
Drug Options: PO Valganciclovir; IV Ganciclovir (Neutropenia risk); IV Foscarnet (Renal toxicity risk); IV Cidofovir (Renal toxicity, uveitis risk).
Local Therapy: Intravitreal injections of ganciclovir and/or foscarnet.

sections.title: Posterior Segment: Toxoplasma & Fungal Infections
content: Toxoplasma Retinochoroiditis: More severe in HIV; often multifocal/bilateral. Moderate/severe vitritis/uveitis. Common neuro-toxo association. Always requires treatment; corticosteroids usually avoided.
Pneumocystis carinii Choroiditis: Bilateral yellow patches (1/4 to 2DD) around posterior pole. Minimal vitritis. Rx: systemic co-trimoxazole or pentamidine.
Cryptococcus Choroiditis: Associated with meningitis. Multifocal off-white lesions ± retinitis/endophthalmitis. Rx: Systemic amphotericin or fluconazole.

sections.title: Immune Recovery & Microvasculopathy
content: Immune Recovery Uveitis (IRU): Paradoxical worsening of inflammation in inactive CMV retinitis as T-cells recover. Features: severe vitritis, TRD, CMO, neovascularization.
Syphilis Choroiditis: Co-infection due to sexual transmission; protean manifestations.
HIV Microvasculopathy: Affects 75%; mechanism unclear (thrombotic vs immune vs direct infection).
Retinal Microvasculopathy signs: Vessel tortuosity, Cotton Wool Spots (CWS), telangiectasia, intraretinal haemorrhages, venous/arterial occlusions.

sections.title: Treatment Safety Warning
content: Neutropenia Risk: Associated with Valganciclovir and IV Ganciclovir.
Renal Toxicity: Major side effect of IV Foscarnet and IV Cidofovir.
Drug-Induced Uveitis: Specifically linked to Cidofovir and Rifabutin therapy.
Steroid Contraindication: Ocular toxoplasmosis in HIV is not normally given with corticosteroids.
